channel.title: The Luverne Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Luverne Journal (luvernejournal.com)

item.title: Second strawberry festival coming March 17
item.description: Second annual CPC Strawberry Festival returns to Luverne March 17, offering homemade strawberry shortcake to raise funds for children's programs, books and scholarships.

item.title: The command was issued
item.description: Rev. R.A. Mathews reflects on Iraq airstrikes, Daniel’s vision, and what the Bible says about heaven, angels, and a God who hears our prayers.

item.title: Turn around, look at me
item.description: A frog fable, a jealous church member, and biblical lessons on ego show why seeking credit can cost more than it gives, and why believers are called to serve for God, not applause.

item.title: Cougars swing into baseball season
item.description: Crenshaw Christian’s young Cougars open the 2026 baseball season under coach Zack Ward, leaning on senior and JV leaders after a 10-0 win and a 13-12 loss.

item.title: Kent arrested after Crenshaw jail inmate overdose
item.description: Luverne man arrested after Crenshaw County jail overdose; deputies say he smuggled drugs that left an inmate unresponsive and now faces contraband and endangerment charges.

item.title: Return to the 'old paths'
item.description: Jeremiah’s call to the “old paths” is applied today as a plea for Christians to leave denominational divisions and return to simple New Testament Christianity.

item.title: Ordinary in our hands, extraordinary in God’s
item.description: A pastor reflects on how God uses ordinary lives — like fishermen, teachers, parents, and mechanics — to do extraordinary work when we place our lives in His hands.

item.title: Mount Zion hosts annual Man Church
item.description: Mount Zion Church in Brantley drew about 125 men from five counties for its annual Man Church worship and fellowship event, with another gathering planned for August.

item.title: Held hostage by hospitality
item.description: Tired of sidewalk small talk? Here’s how to set polite, clear limits with a chatty neighbor — without turning every trip to the mailbox into a 20-minute conversation.

item.title: Pate awarded nutrition school friend of the year
item.description: Alabama Agriculture Commissioner Rick Pate named ASNA Friend of the Year for leading the Farm to School Incentive Program, boosting fresh Alabama-grown foods in cafeterias statewide.
